# Shared options

Contents: [Options](#options), [Target and size](#target-and-size), [Label kinds](#label-kinds), [Value cell](#value-cell), [Annotation anchors](#annotation-anchors).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Every chart type accepts these options unless its own page names them as not accepted. A type page lists the options that are its own, and a path listed there replaces the shared one.

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| target | string | `'report'`, `'dashboard'`, `'slide'`, `'print'` |  | Reading context. Default report. |
| textScale | number |  |  | Text scale; 1 (default) keeps the target sizes, 1.25 sets every text 25 % larger, from 0.5 to 2.5. It scales the width-class size; textSize gives equal text across charts. A factor under 1 stops each text at the target floor. |
| textSize | number |  |  | Primary label size in layout px, 6 to 32, the same at every width; other text keeps its ratio. Not with textScale. |
| a11y | object |  |  | Accessible presentation options; visible chart title is controlled separately by title. |
| a11y.title | boolean |  |  | Emit an SVG title element for hover text; default false. Accessible naming remains available. |
| a11y.table | string | `'hidden'`, `'toggle'`, `'below'` |  | Record-derived accessible data table rendered by the React chart components: 'hidden' keeps it available to assistive technology only, 'toggle' adds a disclosure control, 'below' renders it visibly under the chart. BoardplotChart includes it in the server output; a per-type component adds it after mount. Omitted: no table. The SVG is unchanged. |
| mode | string | `'full'`, `'compact'` |  | Presentation framing. Omitted: full at or above the chart minimum width, compact below it where the type draws there. Compact keeps the title at the theme smallest title size. Some chart-specific schemas use a different mode vocabulary. |
| belowMinimum | string | `'compact'`, `'refuse'` | `'compact'` | What a canvas below the chart minimum gets, on either axis, for the types with a compact floor: `measure` and `boardplot_describe` list it as `compactFloor`. 'compact' (default) draws the tight chart down to the floor: minimal labels, tight spacing, a smaller key, the whole title wrapped, and the subtitle dropped when the plot would be under 80 px. 'refuse' refuses below the minimum. On a canvas with a pinned size, a full-mode refusal for lack of room also falls back to compact under 'compact', and the chart is refused only when compact does not fit either. Types without a compact floor always refuse below their minimum, and every refusal names the minimum it needs. |
| size | string \| object | `'slide-16x9'`, `'slide-4x3'`, `'a4'`, `'dashboard'`, `'a4-landscape-content'`, `'a4-portrait-content'` (or another value of its type) |  | Frame or preset. Defaults: report 720x405 px and dashboard 480x270 px automatic; slide 1184x528 px and print 267x180 mm fixed. Below minimum refuses with a verified size. |
| size.width | number |  |  | Canvas width in the stated unit; at least 100 layout px after conversion. |
| size.height | number |  |  | Canvas height in the stated unit; at least 24 layout px after conversion. Omitted, height stays automatic. |
| size.unit | string | `'px'`, `'pt'`, `'mm'` |  | Dimension unit. Default px. One pt is 96/72 layout px; one mm is 96/25.4 layout px. |
| embed | object |  |  | Declared host display width for readability checks; does not change chart geometry. |
| embed.width | number |  |  | Expected display width in CSS pixels, used to assess effective text size after scaling. |
| margin | object |  |  | Outer canvas margins in pixels; omitted sides use chart or theme defaults. canvas.margin overrides supplied sides. |
| margin.top | number |  |  | Top outer margin in pixels; omission uses chart or theme defaults. |
| margin.right | number |  |  | Right outer margin in pixels; omission uses chart or theme defaults. |
| margin.bottom | number |  |  | Bottom outer margin in pixels; omission uses chart or theme defaults. |
| margin.left | number |  |  | Left outer margin in pixels; omission uses chart or theme defaults. |
| canvas | object |  |  | Canvas framing overrides applied before chart furniture is laid out. |
| canvas.margin | object |  |  | Per-side outer margins overriding margin, then chart or theme defaults. |
| canvas.margin.top | number |  |  | Top outer margin in pixels; omission uses chart or theme defaults. |
| canvas.margin.right | number |  |  | Right outer margin in pixels; omission uses chart or theme defaults. |
| canvas.margin.bottom | number |  |  | Bottom outer margin in pixels; omission uses chart or theme defaults. |
| canvas.margin.left | number |  |  | Left outer margin in pixels; omission uses chart or theme defaults. |
| title | string \| false | `false` (or another value of its type) |  | Visible title override; omission retains the chart-specific title behaviour. |
| subtitle | string \| object |  |  | Measure subtitle below the title; strings expand to the measure field. |
| subtitle.company | string |  |  | Company or scope text before the measure. |
| subtitle.measure | string |  |  | Measure named by the subtitle; options.unit supplies its unit. |
| subtitle.period | string |  |  | Reporting period text after the measure. |
| subtitle.scenarios | array |  |  | Scenario captions in authored order, printed as their own segment joined with "vs": "… · 6 Jul to 4 Oct · AC vs PL". |
| unit | string |  |  | Chart unit, composed into the subtitle where supported; individual series may declare their own units. A unit prints as text after the number, so unit 'USD' reads 2,456 USD. For a currency sign, set format instead, such as '$1,234'; a unit the format already prints warns unit-in-format, and a unit that names another currency than the format's sign warns unit-format-conflict. |
| unitShown | boolean |  |  | True when the host prints the unit beside the chart: no unit line, no unit beside a kpi value; line end labels, a table head and the legend check treat the unit as shown. Number formatting does not change. Default false. |
| source | string |  |  | Source credit rendered in the chart frame. |
| footnotes | array \| false | `false` (or another value of its type) |  | Footnotes in authored order; the frame prints them within notes.maxLines and the rest go to the notes list. false leaves notes and the pointer off the frame; disclosures that notes.show prints, the source line and a required map credit stay. |
| notes | object |  |  | Notes; the footer rule: where the notes under the chart go, how many lines they take, and the note lines for what the drawing leaves out. |
| notes.maxListed | integer \| string | `'all'` (or another value of its type) | `8` | Items a note line names before it counts the rest, such as "Not labelled on the chart: ... and 236 more". Default: every note line names as many items as fit two footer lines, at most 8, reference lines and line end values first, then the rest in data order, and ends with "and N more"; when no name fits, it counts. 'all' names every item. 0 names none and only counts them, "18 of 36 values". All items stay in the reading and the hover records. |
| notes.placement | string | `'frame'`, `'info'`, `'list'` |  | Where the notes go. 'frame' prints notes in the frame within maxLines and the rest in the notes list; 'list' prints only the source line, a required map credit and the pointer; 'info' is the React "Notes and sources" button with one visible line of source and required credit (an SVG or PNG draws it as 'frame'). Default by target: dashboard 'info', slide 'list', report and print 'frame'. |
| notes.maxLines | integer |  |  | Visible lines of notes and source line in the frame; a required map credit and a disclosure do not count. Notes that do not fit go to the notes list and the pointer counts them. Default report and dashboard 3 (2 under 720 px wide), slide 2, print 3. |
| notes.show | string[] | `'note'`, `'method'`, `'disclosure'`, `'ranks'` |  | The kinds of note the frame prints. Default ['note'], the authored footnotes, within maxLines; an authored note a mark points at always prints. 'method' adds the one-line short form of the method notes the engine writes (likert net, pvm split). 'disclosure' adds the engine's notes on how to read the chart (a key, a data change, 'Not labelled on the chart: ...'), outside maxLines; then a chart may also key its marks to them, such as rank numbers under the columns. 'ranks' prints only the rank key: rank numbers under the columns where the names fit neither upright nor rotated, with the note that names them, and no other disclosure. Engine notes print nowhere under the chart by default; every note stays in the notes list of the render result and in its warnings. |
| notes.pointer | boolean |  | `true` | Default true: when the notes list holds notes of the kinds notes.show prints that the frame does not print, the source line ends with "+N notes". |
| theme | string \| object |  |  | Theme preset or preset with overrides; request context may supply it, otherwise resolution uses boardroom. |
| theme.preset | string |  |  | Registered base theme whose tokens are overridden. |
| theme.overrides | object |  |  | Partial theme token tree merged with the named preset. |
| locale | object |  |  | Language and number marks. decimal and thousands set the marks of every number, as in a spreadsheet (default 1,234.5); a format example gives only the shape. language changes words only, never the marks. |
| locale.language | string |  |  | BCP 47 language tag. Changes words only, such as notes and month names. It never changes the decimal or grouping marks; they come only from locale.decimal and locale.thousands. E.g. "de"; "de_DE" is read as "de-DE"; "en-US" puts the month first (Sep 4). |
| locale.decimal | string | `'.'`, `','` |  | Decimal mark of every number the chart prints. Default '.'. The language does not change it. |
| locale.thousands | string | `','`, `'.'`, `'’'`, `' '` |  | Grouping mark of every number the chart prints. Default ',', or '.' with decimal ','. The language does not change it. A value equal to the decimal mark uses that fallback. |
| locale.minusGlyph | string | `'−'`, `'-'` |  | Minus glyph for locale-derived table formats; default Unicode minus. |
| locale.weekStartsOn | number | `0`, `1` |  | First weekday for week-granularity date ticks; default Monday. Line date ticks read this field, other layouts ignore it and report it. |
| strings | object |  |  | Wording of built-in labels. These are the labels the renderer composes itself: author chart text stays unchanged and an explicit option still wins per label; host-level wording comes from the theme provider. |
| strings.newItems | string |  |  | PVM entry-bar name; default New items. |
| strings.lostItems | string |  |  | PVM exit-bar name; default Lost items. |
| strings.cohortMeasure | string |  |  | Cohort measure name for notes, keys and accessible descriptions; default Retention. Use Cumulative conversion for converted counts divided by cohort base. |
| strings.cohortFormula | string |  |  | Complete cohort formula sentence for method notes and accessible descriptions. Wording only: rates still use the count and denominator selected by basis. |
| strings.others | string |  |  | Name of the aggregated rest bucket; default Others, and an explicit topN.restLabel still wins. |
| strings.total | string |  |  | Label of a computed total row; default Total. |
| strings.source | string |  |  | Word introducing the authored source credit; default Source. |
| strings.notApplicable | string |  |  | Not applicable text; n/a, German k. A. |
| strings.legendCount | string |  |  | Legend disclosure wording; '{count}' becomes "2 of 4". Default depends on the legend subject. |
| strings.partial | string |  |  | Word after the labels of partial categories in the column, bar, line and combo footnote, also the hatch key label; default Partial; a named key uses toDate. |
| strings.better | string |  |  | Meaning of a better sign-coloured value. |
| strings.worse | string |  |  | Meaning of a worse sign-coloured value. |
| strings.positiveTotal | string |  |  | Name of a mixed-sign stack positive boundary. |
| strings.rangeMidNote | string |  |  | Range method note. |
| strings.sensitivityNote | string |  |  | Tornado method note. |
| strings.hatchedBaseNote | string |  |  | Tornado base mismatch note. |
| strings.missingSwingNote | string |  |  | Tornado missing output note; {drivers} is replaced. |
| strings.rankOmitted | string |  |  | Focused bump note. |
| strings.noRank | string |  |  | A missing bump rank. |
| strings.rankMethod | string |  |  | Bump method note; {direction}, {format}, and {ring} are replaced. |

| strings.nearZeroNote | string |  |  | Note for folded zero line ends. |

| format | string |  |  | Chart-level format-by-example, such as 1,234.5 or 1.2pp. A currency sign comes from here: '$1,234' prints $2,456. Its decimals are preserved; series and cell formats can override it. Without a format, precision follows the data. A magnitude after the number divides the raw value: k, thousand, Tsd., Tausend (10³); m, M, mn, mm, million(s), Mio., Million(en) (10⁶); b, B, bn, billion(s), Mrd., Milliarde(n), milliard(s) (10⁹); T glued to the number, tn, trillion(s), Bio., Billionen (10¹²). A value of 1000 or more in a scale rolls up and one that would print as 0 rolls down, in the example's spelling; a German or French chart prints its own words (Mrd., Bio.; Md, Bn). A % example expects values in percent units: 3.53 prints 3.53%, a fraction 0.0353 prints 0.04%. A separator followed by exactly three digits after a nonzero integer part is a thousands mark: 1.000 groups thousands with a dot and prints decimals with a comma; write 0.000 for three decimals. |
| detailFields | array |  |  | Label, format, unit and order of the cell details keys, the extra facts a value's hover card lists after it: [{ key: 'deals', label: 'Deals', format: '1,234' }]. Declared keys print first, in this order; a details key it does not declare prints after them, labelled with its key. Default: every key, labelled with itself. |
| detailFields[].key | string |  |  | The details key in the cells. |
| detailFields[].label | string |  |  | Label on the hover card; default the key. |
| detailFields[].format | string |  |  | Format-by-example for number details of this key, such as 1,234 or 0.0%. |
| detailFields[].unit | string |  |  | Unit joined to number details of this key as the marks join it, such as EUR. |
| smallValues | string | `'bound'`, `'zero'`, `'scientific'`, `'p-value'` |  | How an automatic number format prints a nonzero value below its last shown digit. Without a format, each table column and chart series takes one precision from its largest value: two significant digits below 1, at most 4 decimals. bound (default): the bound, <0.01 at two decimals, >−0.01 below zero, <1 for whole numbers; a signed change label keeps its sign, <+0.01; below 0.0001 a value prints in scientific form instead. zero: spreadsheet style, the format's own 0.00. scientific: two significant digits and a power of ten, 1.2 × 10⁻⁹. p-value: every value from 0 to 1 prints as APA 7 writes a p-value, three decimals without the leading zero, .042, and <.001 below; larger values keep the rule above. A format the author sets prints as set. |
| palette | string |  |  | Named identity ramp from theme color.palettes; every chart family takes its data ink from it, while good, bad and highlight stay the theme colours. |
| labelDensity | string | `'full'`, `'smart'`, `'minimal'` |  | Label selection policy, default smart. full: every value label competes for a slot, and a segment value that does not fit its segment moves outside on a leader. smart: as full, but a stacked column or combo segment value prints inside its segment or not at all (where one is wider than its column, the stacked column values step down a size, to the floor; still too wide, none prints), and a segment value drops when the segment is shorter than the label height plus 4 px padding (the label width on a horizontal bar); mekko also drops segment values in columns narrower than 24 px. A labelPlacements pin keeps its label. minimal: keeps only the chart's essential labels (totals, endpoints, highlights). Collision suppression applies at every level. |
| labels | false \| object | `false` (or another value of its type) |  | Label visibility and content overrides; omission uses the selected chart policy. Unsupported chart types refuse this shared option. false turns optional labels off. An object maps a label kind (category, series, segment, point, total, grandTotal, insidePie, outsidePie, percentIndicator, restSeries, tick, axisTitle, valueLine, annotation, growth, activity, item; each chart reads its own, and a kind it does not read is refused) to true, false or content parts from absolute, percent, category and series. On a stacked column with one PY reference series, { growth: false } drops the growth arrows over the totals (↑ 6.1%) and keeps the PY ticks and their labels; { percentIndicator: false } drops the 100% marker of a 100% chart. On bar, box, column, combo, dot, line, Mekko, slope and variance, false keeps category names; { category: false } hides them. On bullet, butterfly, funnel, heatmap, pyramid and status, false keeps the row, column and stage names; on kpi it keeps the main number and the card name. Grid panels can leave category names to the grid. On a line, series false turns the series names off and point sets what each printed value shows, so { point: ['category', 'absolute'] } prints 08-16 44.7 at the point. On a stacked column or combo, { segment: ['absolute', 'percent'] } prints each segment value over its share of the stack; a stack with a negative or missing part prints the value alone and warns. restSeries sets the values of a stacked column, bar or area series whose colorRole is others: absent, they print everywhere except the dashboard target, where the hover card and the note line carry them; true prints them, false hides and notes them on every target. |
| categoryLabels | string | `'axis'`, `'staircase'` |  | Where category names go: 'axis' (default), the row under the axis; 'staircase', each name over the lower columns beside its own, one step lower than the last, with a vertical leader to its column (column, combo, pareto). Without a seat for every name the row returns and staircase-labels-fallback warns. |
| labelPlacements | object |  |  | Authored placement pins keyed by label id; the solver checks each requested slot. On a line, a pinned end label removes the legend step of the end-label ladder. The slots a label can take depend on the chart and its data; a wrong slot warns unknown-slot and lists the valid and free slots of that render. |
| legend | string \| object | `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'none'`, `'auto'` (or another value of its type) |  | A key without a named position sits in one row above the plot, flush with it, under the subtitle; more items wrap to further rows and move the plot down. 'bottom' puts the row under the plot. 'right' is refused: a key beside the plot takes the plot's width. 'auto' adds keys when visible labels do not name every drawn series. A displayed subtitle measure or unit can name one primary series, matching the complete phrase without case sensitivity. Required explanatory keys remain, except the keys of a table, heatmap, cohort and variance, which 'none' drops for a host that draws its own. Automatic keys use footnote type in the top row. Explicit settings override theme.legend.auto, which defaults to false. Multi-series column, bar, combo, dot and scatter charts add a key when direct names are missing. A series key explains its scenario styling. Grids keep a required key under 'none' when direct names are incomplete. |
| legend.position | string | `'top'`, `'bottom'` |  | Key position: 'top', one row above the plot, or 'bottom'. A key beside the plot ('right') is refused. |
| legend.order | array |  |  | Legend item ids in the requested order; unspecified items follow. |
| valueAxis | object |  |  | Value-axis display and domain settings; each chart schema narrows the supported fields. |
| valueAxis.show | boolean |  |  | Draw the value axis with its ticks. Default: shown unless every value is labelled; true keeps it beside the labels, false hides it. |
| valueAxis.min | number |  |  | Requested lower domain bound; chart data can widen it to avoid clipping values. |
| valueAxis.max | number |  |  | Requested upper domain bound; chart data can widen it to avoid clipping values. |
| valueAxis.tickStep | number |  |  | Requested positive tick step. Line and column draw their ticks at the step and snap the domain out to it, never cutting data; box ignores it with a warning, and every other type refuses it because it picks a readable step from the data. |
| valueAxis.includeZero | boolean |  |  | Include zero in the value domain; zero-based marks can require it even when false. |
| valueAxis.percent | boolean |  |  | Request the chart percent-axis or percentage presentation where supported; meanings and support follow the chart-specific schema. |
| valueAxis.log | boolean \| string | `'x'`, `'y'`, `'both'` (or another value of its type) |  | Scatter only: a log10 scale on the horizontal axis ('x'), the vertical axis ('y', also true) or both. Ticks print plain numbers in the chart format at both ends and at 1, 2 and 5 of each decade (3, 4, 6 and 8 too under one decade), down to the decades alone where labels would touch, and the domain ends on the nearest round number past the data, never on a decade the data does not reach. Every value on a log axis must be above zero: a point, cut point, zone, value line, clamp or view bound at or below zero is refused with its path. Every other type refuses the key. |
| valueAxis.reverse | boolean |  |  | Reverse the value-axis direction on line and scatter; box ignores it with a warning, and every other type refuses it. |
| valueAxis.gridlines | boolean |  |  | Show value-axis gridlines where supported; default false. |
| valueAxis.break | string \| false \| object | `'auto'`, `false` (or another value of its type) |  | No break by default or with false. Waterfall and pvm alone accept 'auto' to choose a safe break; { from, to, style? } sets the omitted span. A valid straight break uses a fixed 12px gap and discloses the omitted range. Totals and levels stay visibly longer than smaller steps or segments and no shorter than equal ones. Unsafe automatic breaks move down when valid; unsafe authored breaks are ignored with a warning. An unbroken positive bridge gets an info hint when its smallest total divided by its largest step exceeds 10. |
| valueAxis.break.from | number |  |  | Lower value bounding the omitted domain span. |
| valueAxis.break.to | number |  |  | Upper value bounding the omitted domain span. |
| valueAxis.break.style | string | `'straight'` |  | Break glyph style: 'straight'. |
| categoryAxis | object |  |  | Category-axis settings implemented by line charts; other shared-base charts refuse this option. |
| categoryAxis.crossesBetween | boolean |  |  | Line-chart category placement: default true centres categories in bands; false places the end categories at the plot edges. |
| categoryAxis.dateTicks | string | `'years'`, `'quarters'`, `'months'`, `'weeks'`, `'days'` |  | Line-chart date tick interval. A short tick under the plot marks the first category of each calendar interval. 'years', 'quarters' and 'months' name those ticks on the calendar: quarters read Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct. A row too narrow for every name keeps a larger round step counted from January (years 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50 or 100, so every tenth year from 1980; quarters 2, 4, 8, 20 or 40; months 2, 3, 6, 12, 24, 60 or 120), at most eight names. The latest period is always named; if it collides with the tick before it, that tick drops. 'weeks' and 'days' count equal steps back from the latest period (weeks 2, 4, 13, 26 or 52; days 2, 7, 14 or 28) and name it too. 'years' names the year alone ('Jan 1980' reads 1980) where the label carries it. 'months' over day dates the engine labels names the month ('1 Apr 2025' reads Apr 2025, then May, Jun). A monthly series through July 2026 with 'years' reads 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, Jul 2026. Without dateTicks, column, stacked column, line, area and combo pick tick months by the same calendar rule for rows of months and quarters (step 3: Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct; step 6: Jan, Jul; step 12: Jan; plus the latest period) and count back from the latest period for days and weeks, so side-by-side panels with the same categories show the same months. A line or area day row that would step past 28 days names months as 'months' does. Categories without an ISO date leave the option unused and report date-ticks-unsupported. |
| secondaryAxis | object |  |  | Opt in to a second value scale on supported charts; combo adds chart-specific secondary-axis options. |
| secondaryAxis.acknowledge | true | `true` |  | Explicitly acknowledge that the chart uses an independent second value scale. |
| scaleGroup | object |  |  | Scale-group identities for panel composition. Charts of one envelope that name the same y group draw on one domain, and a chart that cannot join (another unit, no numeric y scale) refuses the request. A chart alone in its group, or a single chart, keeps its own scale for the host to share. x is refused: no chart type shares an x scale. |
| scaleGroup.y | string |  |  | Shared value-scale group id for compatible grid panels, charts of one envelope or separately mounted cards; members of the same group use a combined domain. |
| scaleGroup.id | string |  |  | Stable member id inside the scale group declared on the host ScaleGroup; reordering or removing cards does not change which member this chart is. |
| rowLabels | object |  |  | Row-label alignment for the horizontal families (bar, bullet, box, dot, likert). |
| rowLabels.align | string | `'left'`, `'right'` |  | Row-label alignment on a horizontal category axis; defaults to 'left' (one shared left edge), and to 'right' on a dot chart. 'right' pushes each label block against the plot. |
| sort | object |  |  | Sorting requests for charts that support them; omitted settings preserve the chart default ordering. |
| sort.categories | string | `'sheet'`, `'asc'`, `'desc'`, `'reverse'` |  | Category order: sheet preserves authored order, reverse reverses it, asc and desc use the chart category ranking value. |
| sort.segments | string | `'sheet'`, `'asc'`, `'desc'`, `'reverse'` |  | Segment order: sheet preserves authored order, reverse reverses it, asc and desc use the chart segment ranking value. |
| topN | object |  |  | Chart-specific Top-N selection and rest aggregation; omission retains all categories. On a choropleth world map, topN.n picks the n regions it labels, largest absolute value first; other maps label every region. |
| topN.n | integer |  |  | Maximum number of individually retained categories after chart-specific ranking. |
| topN.rest | boolean |  |  | Aggregate remaining categories into a rest bucket by default; false omits them where supported. On a bar mekko the rest bucket is the width-weighted mean of its rates. Pareto retains the bucket to preserve its population. |
| topN.restLabel | string |  |  | Authored rest-bucket name; ordinary charts default to Others and Pareto to Rest. |
| topN.showRestCount | boolean |  |  | Append the number of aggregated categories; ordinary charts default to false, while Pareto always discloses the count. |
| topN.threshold | number |  |  | Bar-chart minimum absolute category total after the rank cut; not a universal Top-N threshold. Pareto warns that it ignores this field. |
| bandFraction | number |  |  | Fraction of a category band occupied by its mark, greater than zero and at most one; default is chart-specific, commonly 0.7. |
| highlight | string \| array |  |  | One or more data ids selected for chart-specific visual emphasis. Selected marks take color.focus, and color.highlight on a theme that sets no focus. On a single-series bar, column or dot chart the named categories take it and every other mark steps back to color.neutralLight, the rest role. A series fill or colorRole outranks both colours; scenario marks keep their pattern and signColor its good/bad colours, and unhighlighted scenario marks keep their scenario colour. A highlight with no visible mark (null, or a zero bar or column) recedes nothing. On a line the named series take it at 2.6px and the others step through muted tints toward ink, with a swatch on each end label. On an unstacked area with several series the first named series is the one that is filled. |
| story | object |  |  | Guided steps over one chart. Each step fades the marks it does not name and shows a panel with its title and body. React needs withStory from boardplot/react/story. |
| story.steps | array |  |  | Steps in order. |
| story.steps[].id | string |  |  | Step id, as the React step prop names it. |
| story.steps[].title | string |  |  | Panel title. |
| story.steps[].body | string |  |  | Panel text. |
| story.steps[].highlight | string \| array |  |  | Data ids the step brings forward, as in highlight; the other marks fade. Omitted: an intro. |
| story.step | string |  |  | Step static output draws; default the first. |
| focus | object \| null |  |  | Active source focus: labels whose owner the focus selects sort ahead in the solve order, because the focus adds a 250-point bonus to the label's sort key on top of its authored priority. The bonus can carry a focused label past a higher authored band, which is the point: a focused series or category wins contested label space. Layout only — totals, shares, scales and claims are unchanged, and a focused label still loses to the density gate, to an owned pin and to a collision. Omit the key (or set null) for byte-identical layout; null clears an inherited focus explicitly. On a grid, set it on the panel options that own the focus; sibling panels are separate layouts and never see it. |
| focus.owner | object |  |  | Source owner to emphasise. A label is selected when its own owner carries every key named here with the same value, so a seriesId alone selects that series and a seriesId+categoryId pair selects one point. |
| focus.owner.seriesId | string |  |  | Source series identity. |
| focus.owner.categoryId | string |  |  | Source category identity. |
| focus.owner.segmentId | string |  |  | Source segment identity. |
| focus.owner.pointId | string |  |  | Source point identity. |
| focus.owner.valueLineId | string |  |  | Source value-line identity. |
| focus.owner.annotationId | string |  |  | Source annotation identity. |
| focus.owner.rowId | string |  |  | Source table row identity. |
| focus.owner.colId | string |  |  | Source table column identity. |
| hatchStrength | number |  |  | How strongly forecast, partial-period and no-data hatches draw, 0 to 100; 100 is the theme's recipe. Lower values fade the stripes toward their ground and, on a line or area forecast, spread them up to 2.5 times the theme's gap. The fade stops at a floor: where the hatch is the only cue (a forecast column or bar, a partial period, a no-data cell) the stripes keep 3:1 on their ground and their spacing; on a line or area forecast, where the dashed line, the divider and the key already mark the forecast, they keep 2:1. A status cell lays its stripes on its own tone: there 60 is the theme's recipe at 3:1, 100 deepens the stripes to 4.5:1 on the same ground, and lower values fade them only as far as the cell stays apart from a cell with no status. Default 60 on a line or area forecast and a status cell, 100 elsewhere. The key swatch draws the same hatch. |
| colorblindSafe | boolean |  |  | Paint the semantic good/bad pair from theme.color.colorblind, a pair told apart without red and green: signed bars and columns, variance bars, status cells, heatmap valence cells, table tones, heat grounds, in-cell bars and badges, and the poles of a diverging choropleth or tilemap scale. Other types refuse this option. Use palette for categorical colours. |
| rounding | string | `'nearest'`, `'sum-consistent'` |  | How computed shares print. nearest rounds each share separately. sum-consistent uses largest remainders to total 100%. For equal remainders, when the sum must go up, round up the smaller share first; when the sum must go down, take the step from the larger share first. Equal-size ties use the first input index. reading.rounding lists changes. Use format: 1.0% for one decimal. Mekko cell, series and chart share formats set the precision. Bar, column and combo stacks default to sum-consistent for each complete stack; a column's shares keep the chart's one share precision or shareLabels.format. Incompatible precisions or more than 13 decimals warn and keep the requested formats without sum-consistent rounding. |
| animate | boolean |  |  | Reserved motion flag; registered charts currently refuse it because the engine emits static geometry. |
| interactive | boolean |  |  | Emit data-bp-* semantics for dependency-free web interactivity; static output is unchanged by default. |
| debug | boolean |  |  | Reserved layout debug flag; registered charts refuse it. |
| annotations | array |  |  | Data-bound annotations in authored order; explicit ids must be unique and each chart advertises its supported kinds. |
| annotations[].kind (annotations[] branch 1) | string | `'diff'`, `'cagr'`, `'delta'`, `'abs'`, `'note'`, `'callout'`, `'valueLine'`, `'indicator100'`, `'event'` |  | Annotation operation; its anchors and additional fields are checked by the chart annotation pass. |
| annotations[].id (annotations[] branch 1) | string |  |  | Stable annotation identity; omission generates an id from kind and authored order. |
| annotations[].text (annotations[] branch 1) | string |  |  | Authored annotation text; refused on valueLine, which prints label, and on indicator100. ${value} prints the computed number in it: a cagr's rate with its suffix, a diff's change, a delta's difference, the anchored value of an abs, note or callout. Without ${value}, text on a cagr, diff, delta or abs replaces the number, warns annotation-authored-override and the claim record marks the override. |
| annotations[].format (annotations[] branch 1) | string |  |  | Number format: annotation > anchored series > chart. Diff uses to, then from. CAGR and relative/reversed diff need a percent example; value differences use pp for percent levels. Refused on event and indicator100. |
| annotations[].priority (annotations[] branch 1) | number |  |  | Annotation label priority during collision resolution. |
| annotations[].icon (annotations[] branch 1) | string | `'alert'`, `'calendar'`, `'check'`, `'conversation'`, `'document'`, `'flag'`, `'gear'`, `'lightbulb'`, `'people'`, `'star'`, `'target'`, `'workflow'` |  | Registered icon for note or callout annotations; cannot be combined with status. |
| annotations[].status (annotations[] branch 1) | string | `'good'`, `'bad'`, `'warn'`, `'info'` |  | Semantic status glyph for a note or callout; cannot be combined with icon. |
| annotations[].shape (annotations[] branch 1) | string | `'bracket'`, `'arrow'` |  | A cagr's form: 'bracket', the default, runs over the marks, and 'arrow' is one straight arrow with the rate in an oval on it. |
| annotations[].kind (annotations[] branch 2) | string | `'band'` |  | Era band spanning inclusive category ids, or a value-axis plan corridor, tolerance band or attainment fill. |
| annotations[].id (annotations[] branch 2) | string |  |  | Stable band annotation identity; omission generates an id from kind and authored order. |
| annotations[].text (annotations[] branch 2) | string |  |  | Shared annotation text override; band captions use label. |
| annotations[].format (annotations[] branch 2) | string |  |  | Shared annotation value format; the band caption itself is authored text. |
| annotations[].priority (annotations[] branch 2) | number |  |  | Band label priority during collision resolution. |
| annotations[].from (annotations[] branch 2) | string |  |  | First category included in the band; required for era shade/bracket, optional clip for value-axis bands. |
| annotations[].to (annotations[] branch 2) | string |  |  | Last category included in the band; required for era shade/bracket, optional clip for value-axis bands. |
| annotations[].label (annotations[] branch 2) | string |  |  | Optional period or corridor label. |
| annotations[].tone (annotations[] branch 2) | string | `'neutral'`, `'muted'` |  | Semantic era-band tone; both use the theme others tint. Refused on corridor, tolerance and attainment. |
| annotations[].style (annotations[] branch 2) | string | `'shade'`, `'bracket'`, `'corridor'`, `'tolerance'`, `'attainment'` |  | Band presentation; 'shade' is the default category tint, 'bracket' is a double-headed period arrow, 'corridor' is a plan value band, 'tolerance' is an authored value range, 'attainment' shades actual versus plan. |
| annotations[].divider (annotations[] branch 2) | false \| string | `false`, `'start'`, `'end'`, `'both'` |  | Optional dashed divider at one or both bracket-band edges; other band styles refuse this field. |
| annotations[].low (annotations[] branch 2) | number |  |  | Lower value-axis bound for corridor and tolerance bands. |
| annotations[].high (annotations[] branch 2) | number |  |  | Upper value-axis bound for corridor and tolerance bands. |
| annotations[].value (annotations[] branch 2) | number |  |  | Plan value for attainment shading; actuals are resolved per category. |
| annotations[].seriesId (annotations[] branch 2) | string |  |  | Series whose actuals are shaded for attainment; omission uses the category total. |
| annotations[].scenario (annotations[] branch 2) | string | `'AC'`, `'PY'`, `'PL'`, `'FC'` |  | Scenario notation for a plan corridor; default PL. |
| annotations[].direction (annotations[] branch 2) | string | `'higherIsBetter'`, `'lowerIsBetter'` |  | Whether exceeding the plan is favorable for attainment shading; default higherIsBetter. |

Set `locale.decimal` (and optionally `locale.thousands`) to choose the marks of every number in the chart, as in a spreadsheet. The default is `1,234.5` in every language; `locale.language` changes words only, never the marks. Format examples give only the shape; `1.2%` and `1,2 %` both mean one decimal; `1,2 %` keeps its space and prints `1.2 %` by default.

## Target and size

`target` names the medium the chart is read in and `size` its slot. `report` is the default. `size` takes a preset or `{ width, height, unit }` with `unit` `px` (the default), `pt` or `mm`; the engine converts to layout px (1 pt is 96/72 px, 1 mm is 96/25.4 px) and does not round. A preset sets the size, not the target. A target given to the CLI, the MCP call or a React prop wins over `options.target`. A grid passes its target to its panels; a panel cannot choose another. [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing) gives the slot size for each medium, the type sizes and the display rules.

| `activity` | [gantt](gantt.md) |

| `percentIndicator` | [bar](bar.md), [column](column.md), [line](line.md) |
| `point` | [bar](bar.md), [box](box.md), [bullet](bullet.md), [butterfly](butterfly.md), [cohort](cohort.md), [column](column.md), [combo](combo.md), [dot](dot.md), [funnel](funnel.md), [heatmap](heatmap.md), [histogram](histogram.md), [kpi](kpi.md), [line](line.md), [pareto](pareto.md), [pyramid](pyramid.md), [scatter](scatter.md), [variance](variance.md) |

## Value cell

Series values and most data values take a cell. A number, null (missing), or an object with one of number, pct (50.5 means 50.5%) or date (ISO 8601), plus optional fill, format, label (text or false), priority, scenario (AC|PY|PL|FC), footnote and, on range types, range {low, high, mid}.

## Annotation anchors

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.
